questions.correctFeedback: Right — the barcode is (q + pe^t)^n, so p goes with e^t: p = 0.7, n = 10.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Match (q + pe^t)^n: the number beside e^t is p = 0.7, the other is q = 0.3, and the power is n = 10.

questions.correctFeedback: Yes — that's the Poisson(4) barcode, and a Poisson's variance equals λ.
questions.incorrectFeedback: e^(λ(e^t − 1)) is Poisson(λ); here λ = 4, and Var = λ = 4.

questions.stem: X ~ Bin(5, p) and Y ~ Bin(7, p) are independent. X + Y is…
questions.incorrectFeedback: Multiply the MGFs: (q + pe^t)^5(q + pe^t)^7 = (q + pe^t)^12, the Bin(12, p) barcode.

questions.stem: Which rule needs X and Y to be independent?
questions.correctFeedback: Right — E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y] always holds; M_{X+Y} = M_X M_Y needs independence.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Linearity of means never needs independence (L6). The product rule for MGFs does: with Y = X it fails.

questions.stem: From Lesson 10: each try succeeds with chance 1/3. P(no success in the first 2 tries) is…
questions.incorrectFeedback: Both tries must fail: q² = (2/3)² = 4/9. 1/9 is both succeeding.
